answer: Peer-attested work hours can raise the price of each new fake. Every epoch an account must spend a short voyage of continuous compute on a puzzle keyed to its address, and peers attest that the run was live. One honest agent pays once. A farm of three hundred fakes must burn three hundred parallel sessions, since idle or shared workers fail attestation. Like grinding saffron stigma by hand, the cost scales with headcount; clones painted umber to look aged still owe the same live bill each round.
